title: Game definition: Global Thermonuclear War
description:
A playable implementation inspired by the movie WarGames. Asymmetric 2-player (USA/USSR) simultaneous nuclear strategy game. Players secretly allocate missiles to targets and ABM defenses, then launch simultaneously. Imperfect information: opponent targeting hidden until launch phase. The game demonstrates that optimal play always produces mutual destruction — the only winning move is not to play.

Features exercised: simultaneous phases (commit-reveal), hidden visibility, fog of war, graph zone (world map), counter zones (missiles/ABM stockpiles), multiple phases (deploy/target/launch/resolve/assess), end conditions (survival threshold — if both sides destroyed, draw).

Design: ~20 target cities per side with population values. Missile types: ICBM (high damage, slow), SLBM (medium damage, fast), bomber (low damage, recallable). ABM defense: limited interceptors per city. Targeting is simultaneous sealed orders. Resolution: each missile vs ABM intercept probability, surviving missiles destroy target. Victory: side with more surviving population wins, but mutual destruction (both below threshold) is a draw with the message 'A strange game. The only winning move is not to play.'
close_reason: 59th game definition: 40 cities (20/side), simultaneous sealed orders, commit-reveal launch, ABM intercept resolution, mutual destruction draw. 52 Python tests. 'The only winning move is not to play.'
